About the job
Google's software engineers develop the next-generation technologies that change how billions of users connect, explore, and interact with information and one another. Our products need to handle information at massive scale, and extend well beyond web search. We're looking for engineers who bring fresh ideas from all areas, including information retrieval, distributed computing, large-scale system design, networking and data storage, security, artificial intelligence, natural language processing, UI design and mobile; the list goes on and is growing every day. We need our engineers to be versatile, display leadership qualities and be enthusiastic to take on new problems across the full-stack as we continue to push technology forward.
Modern applications are architected as distributed collections of microservices. A service mesh is a dedicated infrastructure layer for transparently adding capabilities like observability, traffic management, and security. The CSM (Cloud Service Mesh) Platform is a critical component of Google Cloud's Service Centric Networking, acting as the foundation for AI enablements and next-generation Agentic workloads. Our mission is to create many differentiating features to allow customers to operate their microservices securely, compliantly, and scalably, regardless of the platform they run on or the type of compute infrastructure they need.
Google Cloud accelerates every organization’s ability to digitally transform its business and industry. We deliver enterprise-grade solutions that leverage Google’s cutting-edge technology, and tools that help developers build more sustainably. Customers in more than 200 countries and territories turn to Google Cloud as their trusted partner to enable growth and solve their most critical business problems.

As a Staff Research Data Scientist (Tech Lead) you will define the technical goal, drive applied research agendas, and lead the technical execution of machine learning, deep learning, and generative AI initiatives across Google SecOps, Google Threat Intelligence, and other key cybersecurity product areas in Google Cloud.
In this role, you will manage high-ambiguity, adversarial security problems at Google scale. You will act as the principal research driver and technical lead across initiatives such as agentic security operations, threat intelligence reasoning and contextualization, security-specialized LLMs/foundation models, and dark web threat detection. As a Tech Lead, you will bridge the gap between breakthrough AI research and enterprise-grade deployment: architecting novel research prototypes, steering data strategy, aligning roadmaps with cross-functional SWE and Product leaders, and mentoring junior researchers. You will represent Google's security research externally through high-impact publications, patents, and conference presentations, shaping how the broader AI Security industry defends against advanced threat actors.

About the job
As an organization, Google maintains a portfolio of research projects driven by fundamental research, new product innovation, product contribution and infrastructure goals, while providing individuals and teams the freedom to emphasize specific types of work. As a Research Scientist, you'll setup large-scale tests and deploy promising ideas quickly and broadly, managing deadlines and deliverables while applying the latest theories to develop new and improved products, processes, or technologies. From creating experiments and prototyping implementations to designing new architectures, our research scientists work on real-world problems that span the breadth of computer science, such as machine (and deep) learning, data mining, natural language processing, hardware and software performance analysis, improving compilers for mobile platforms, as well as core search and much more.
As a Research Scientist, you'll also actively contribute to the wider research community by sharing and publishing your findings, with ideas inspired by internal projects as well as from collaborations with research programs at partner universities and technical institutes all over the world.
Our mission is to combine Gemini foundation models with physical intelligence so general-purpose robots can understand and act reliably in the real world. Critical to achieving this goal is obtaining high-quality training data and effectively integrating it into the Gemini training process. Our team's research develops data quality insights on how to best extract physical and action knowledge from robot-related datasets, and incorporates these insights into Gemini pre-training through model training and upstreaming. By pairing data ablations with fast closed-loop robot evaluations, you will shape how physical reasoning and action capabilities emerge in next-generation Gemini models and deploy onto real-world robots.
Artificial intelligence will be one of humanity’s most transformative inventions. At Google DeepMind, we are a pioneering AI lab with exceptional interdisciplinary teams focused on advancing AI development to solve complex global challenges and accelerate high-quality product innovation for billions of users. We use our technologies for widespread public benefit and scientific discovery, ensuring safety and ethics are always our highest priority.
We are pushing the boundaries across multiple domains. Our global teams offer diverse learning opportunities and varied career pathways for those driven to achieve exceptional results through collective effort.

Responsibilities
Develop data quality, filtering, and labeling methodologies, and optimize multimodal data representations and mixtures to upstream physical and action knowledge into Gemini pre-training.
Design and run pre-training and policy training ablations, improve training recipes, and systematically hill-climb physical reasoning and action performance against benchmarks.
Build and maintain the research software, evaluation tools, and lightweight post-training workflows required to iterate on research ideas quickly and verify upstream data quality through offline and closed-loop robot policy evaluations.
Contribute to our wider research agenda—including vision-language-action (VLA) modeling, world-action models, reinforcement learning, and simulation—and communicate findings clearly in a fast-paced, collaborative team environment.

About the job
At Google, research-focused Software Engineers are embedded throughout the company, allowing them to setup large-scale tests and deploy promising ideas quickly and broadly. Ideas may come from internal projects as well as from collaborations with research programs at partner universities and technical institutes all over the world.
From creating experiments and prototyping implementations to designing new architectures, engineers work on real-world problems including artificial intelligence, data mining, natural language processing, hardware and software performance analysis, improving compilers for mobile platforms, as well as core search and much more. But you stay connected to your research roots as an active contributor to the wider research community by partnering with universities and publishing papers.
Engineers on the Polaris team design tasks that test Gemini’s ability to complete software engineering work. A task is essentially an in-depth examination that evaluates how well Gemini performs in a specific, complex scenario. The primary components of a task are: a prompt that instructs Gemini what to do and a grader or rubric that assigns a numerical score to the model’s attempted solution.
Our team, Polaris, is distinguished primarily by how much manual effort we put into building individual eval tasks. Rather than generating a large number of tasks using a synthetic data pipeline, engineers on the Polaris team prioritize creating a smaller number of tasks that more closely capture the realism and complexity of real-world software engineering. A single well-designed task typically takes a Polaris engineer roughly one week to complete, from the initial ideation stage to final approval.
There are no education or degree requirements for this role. No prior work experience is required.
Artificial intelligence will be one of humanity’s most transformative inventions. Gmail Trust and Compliance Infrastructure's mission is to build and maintain infrastructure to keep Gmail and Chat data secure, and to enable rapid development of GenAI based features in Gmail, Workspace and across Google.

Our mission is to meaningfully connect people so they can create, build, and grow together and as part of the team you can build how productivity tools should work 5-10 years into the future. You will work with model builders (Google DeepMind), work with exceptional leaders, and have the ability to impact billions of users across the world.
